subject: APL
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Foundations of Applied Logistics Execution
courses.description: Introduces students to the tactics of logistics and distribution.Explores application of fundamentals in the context of modern consumer expectations: endless shelf, immediate access, expanded notion of the last mile that includes delivery anywhere.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Warehouse Management
courses.description: Introduces students to all aspects of warehouse management, from physical design to automation decisions to using data for capacity planning and optimization.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Freight Management
courses.description: Introduces students to all aspects of freight management, carrier selection and management, rates, billing, decision analysis, rules, regulations, and transportation management systems. Emphasizes data use for optimization.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: ERP Systems for Inventory Management
courses.description: Covers the basics of enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and inventory management, with hands-on tactics of product visibility for day-to-day operations. Focuses on inventory management technology and the organizational structure needed to support different channel networks in logistics.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Supplier Management
courses.description: Covers tactics in managing suppliers for the day-to-day operations, including supplier appraisal, price and contract negotiations, supplier audits, supplier quality and delivery, and e-procurement.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Advanced Technology in Logistics and Distribution
courses.description: Explores the latest technology development and how it applies to logistics and distribution science. Introduces concepts of emerging technologies and their use and purpose. Topics include the Internet-of-things (IoT) and its application in logistics, integrating IoT and cloud computing, machine learning applications, and the issues and challenges with new technology adoption.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Elective
courses.description: Offers elective credit for courses taken at other academic institutions. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Applied Logistics Capstone
courses.description: Offers students, working as individuals or in groups, an opportunity to design and carry out an interdisciplinary project conducted with real-world clients. Students apply strategic frameworks and best practices to help organizations improve logistics operations. Emphasizes the role of digital transformation, applied analytics, and the ability of digital technologies to help solve for disruptions in distribution and warehousing networks.

courses.subject: APL
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Offers students an opportunity to apply knowledge and skills gained through their master’s program to work on challenging short‐term special topics under faculty supervision. Students complete a project/research in which they examine a relevant problem of practice in logistics and supply chain, conduct research, analyze data, and present their findings. Topics may vary from semester to semester.
